messages:
maria_cs: Heads-up — NovaHealth onboarding is seeing a burst of 429s right after we flipped mTLS for their browser SDK. Spike aligns with a ton of OPTIONS preflights. Anyone seen this exact pattern?

devon_engineer: Hmm. Do you have a small sample of the request/headers and the UA? Often preflight parallelism from single-page apps + frequent token rotation can look like a fanout. :eyes:

maria_cs: Pasting sanitized preflight log (options only) — these are all within the same 30s window:
```
OPTIONS /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Origin: https://app.novahealth.com
Access-Control-Request-Method: POST
Access-Control-Request-Headers: content-type, x-nh-ephemeral-token
User-Agent: NovaWeb/1.2.3
x-forwarded-for: 18.212.45.66
```
Also they're rotating ephemeral tokens from a worker every ~8-12s for each tab.

kevin_infra: The gateway enforces combined rate windows: per-api-key AND per-client-ip AND per-route OPTIONS burst caps. If tokens rotate rapidly you get many preflights that still map to the same IP but different key ids — that can trip the per-ip burst even when per-key looks fine.

alyssa_se: So two levers: reduce preflight frequency (CORS caching) OR reduce token rotation fanout. They currently issue a new ephemeral for every in-flight request. :thinking_face:

devon_engineer: Quick mitigations we can suggest to customer:
- Add caching for preflight: `Access-Control-Max-Age: 86400` on the OPTIONS response so browsers skip repeated preflights.
- Use longer-lived session tokens for browser flows (rotate on session/heartbeat instead of per-request).
- If using multiple iframe/workers, consolidate token refresh to a single coordinator.
Example headers we can share: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.novahealth.com`, `Access-Control-Allow-Methods: POST, OPTIONS`, `Access-Control-Max-Age: 86400`.

maria_cs: Can we apply a temporary per-account override so NovaHealth gets a higher OPTIONS burst and we avoid throttling while they change their client? They are on a short timeline for prod.

kevin_infra: I can put a short-lived policy in place: increase OPTIONS burst window for account `acct_novahealth` and pin their observed IP (18.212.45.66) to a higher burst limit for 24h while they remediate client behavior. I'll also enable more verbose preflight logging to watch for regressions.

onboard-bot: Policy change applied by @kevin_infra: `options_burst_increase` for acct_novahealth (expires in 24h).

maria_cs: Awesome — I'll tell them to hold off on super-frequent ephemeral rotations and add the CORS header. Also schedule a follow-up tomorrow. :thumbsup:

devon_engineer: I'll draft a small snippet for docs and an examples repo commit showing how to reuse ephemeral tokens across tabs + set `Access-Control-Max-Age`. Will post PR and ping here.

alyssa_se: I'll run a short enablement call tomorrow 10:00am PT with NovaHealth. Prep checklist: sample code to consolidate refresh, recommended CORS headers, and our logs to show before/after. On it. :spiral_calendar:
